1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: dmso (well A1 in slot 4)
   line 43:  p300.aspirate(60, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 43 the tip went into dmso (well A1 in slot 4) while it still carried compound 1
   (tube A1 in slot 3) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a
   little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does
   not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the unwanted material along into 36
   other wells: wells B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, C1, C2 and 10 more in slot 1; wells B1, B2,
   B3, B4, B5, B6, C1, C2 and 10 more in slot 2.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 4.
   Also reached 36 other wells: wells B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, C1, C2 and 10 more in slot 1;
   wells B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, C1, C2 and 10 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 43 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194

5. WARNING UNMIXED-AT-END: 24 wells never mixed after compound 1, dmso, compound 2, compound
3 and 1 more went in (10% of the well)
   line 206:  p20.dispense(10, plate_assay[src])
   At line 206 the robot added compound 1, dmso, compound 2, compound 3 and 1 more to wells
   A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 2, which already held medium (this
   line did it 24 times). The addition was 10% of the well, nothing mixed the well
   afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do
   not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated.
   The liquid added last is a sample, so nothing else in the workflow will mix it: a
   normalisation or a pool left like this is not what it says it is.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 2 after line 206:
   `mix_after=(5, 80)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 80, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: dmso (well A1 in slot 4)
findings.explanation: At line 43 the tip went into dmso (well A1 in slot 4) while it still carried compound 1 (tube A1 in slot 3) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the unwanted material along into 36 other wells: wells B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, C1, C2 and 10 more in slot 1; wells B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, C1, C2 and 10 more in slot 2.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 43 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: 24 wells never mixed after compound 1, dmso, compound 2, compound 3 and 1 more went in (10% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 206 the robot added compound 1, dmso, compound 2, compound 3 and 1 more to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 2, which already held medium (this line did it 24 times). The addition was 10% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. The liquid added last is a sample, so nothing else in the workflow will mix it: a normalisation or a pool left like this is not what it says it is.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 2 after line 206: `mix_after=(5, 80)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 80, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
